messages:
june: Hey team — I have a conflict for next Wed's crossfunc roadmap sync. Can someone take agenda ownership for this one? Quick proposed agenda (draft):

1) RFC review: router fallback policy (ashok) — 25m
2) Design review: batching/cache console UX (marco) — 20m
3) Priority triage: Dedicated capacity spike mitigation (elaine) — 15m

Proposed timebox total: 60m. Docs: https://redwood.dev/rfc/router-fallback and https://redwood.dev/design/batching-cache-ux

If you take ownership, please: claim the slot, add 1–2 bullet pre-reads to the doc, and mark any decisions we need to capture in the decision log. If no one can, I can move items into separate quick sessions.

ashok: I can own the RFC review. Heads up — the fallback options table needs an extra 5m to cover compatibility checks with quantized variants. Would prefer 30m for the RFC.

marco: I can do the design review but ask that folks skim the mockups before the sync. I've added a "pre-read" section in the design doc with highlights. Also I think the UX discussion tends to run long — can we aim to keep concrete acceptance criteria only? Suggest 25m if we shave elsewhere.

elaine: I want the triage to be focused on the Dedicated spike — we have a customer incident note and a proposed auto-fallback rule. If we can't fit it, I'd rather pull triage into a 30-min follow-up with infra/ops. I can add the incident summary to the triage doc. Also +1 to capturing a decision owner for the fallback rule.

sam: If ashok needs 30m and marco wants 25m that's already 55m, which leaves little room for triage. Options: 1) extend to 75m, 2) move triage to separate 30m slot, 3) host a pre-sync async read and only cover decisions in the meeting. My vote is option 2 + async pre-read.

product-bot: calendar draft created: "Crossfunc Roadmap Sync — Wed 11:00-12:00" — attendees: product, eng, infra. 

calendar-bot: (reaction :calendar:) booked provisional slot and attached draft agenda: https://calendar.redwood/s/roadmap-sync-wed

june: Thanks — sounds like we're leaning toward splitting. Two action items: 1) ashok/marco please add final time requests to the agenda doc by EOD today, 2) elaine please prepare the incident summary and a one-line proposed rollback/fallback rule so the follow-up can be decision-focused. I'll update the calendar to two back-to-back slots if needed.

ashok: ack. I'll update the RFC with the compatibility table and mark decision owner as @ashok.

marco: ack, added acceptance criteria and a short list of UI questions under "pre-read". Marking decision owner for UI changes as @marco.

elaine: added incident summary and proposed rule (one-liner). If we split, I'm fine with a follow-up ad-hoc at Thu 10am.

june: Cool. Final question — who wants to own the meeting notes/decision-log entry downstream? We should capture: final fallback policy, UI acceptance criteria, and triage action items.

ashok: I'll draft the decision-log entry after the RFC portion. Posting suggested entry here:

```
Decision: Router fallback policy v1
Owner: ashok
Summary: default to smaller model variant with KV-cache warmup and 5% canary traffic for 48h. If errors > 1% revert to previous stable variant and page infra.
Date: 2026-03-18
Related: https://redwood.dev/decisions/router-fallback
```

marco: I'll add the UI acceptance criteria to the decision log (short bullets).

june: Perfect — thanks all. I'll split the calendar and finalize times by EOD. If anyone sees a hard blocker, ping me directly. :thumbsup:
